approachQuestion.prompt: A display sequence is defined by T(0)=0, T(1)=1, and T(k)=T(k−1)+T(k−2) for k≥2. Return T(n) modulo 1000000007. Examples: n=0 returns 0; n=1 returns 1; n=6 returns 8. Which method best handles repeated subproblems for the full input range?
constraints: Arithmetic on residues and table access each take constant time.

options.text: Use a recursive helper for T(k). Return the stored value when k is already computed; otherwise compute the two smaller values, store their sum modulo the modulus, and return it.
options.feedback: Each index is computed once, while the recursive definition and cached results agree with the base values.

options.text: Start with the values for indices 0 and 1, then advance from k=2 through n, keeping only the previous two residues.
options.feedback: This bottom-up method computes the same sequence and is also an optimal choice for returning only one value.

options.text: Return the recursive sum of calls for k−1 and k−2 without storing any previously computed result.
options.feedback: The result is correct, but the same smaller indices are recomputed across many branches.

options.text: Return only the recursive result for k−1, adding the base values when k is small.
options.feedback: The recurrence requires both preceding values. For n=3, following only k−1 yields 1 instead of 2.

feedback.reason: Cache by recurrence index, not by call occurrence.
details: The recursive helper returns 0 for index 0 and 1 for index 1. For any larger index, it first checks the cache. If absent, it obtains the two preceding residues, adds them modulo 1000000007, stores the result at the current index, and returns it. The analyzed method begins with an empty cache and calls the helper for n.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For memo-recursion, choose the worst-case time and auxiliary-space costs in terms of n. Count the cache and active recursive call stack; exclude the input integer and returned residue.

feedback.reason: Memoization computes each index once and retains both cache and active calls.
details: The cache ensures that each index from 0 through n is completed once, with constant work per completed index. The cache stores a linear number of residues, and a first descent can keep a linear number of recursive calls active.
“O(2^n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: That bound fits the uncached recursive tree. With memoization, a completed index is reused instead of expanding its subproblem again.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The running time matches, but this recursive method keeps cached residues and active calls that grow with n.
“O(1) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: The recursive dependency chain must reach the requested index, so the method cannot finish in constant time for growing n.
